sentences.text:
This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 28.10.2021.
2.

The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 28.10.2021 at about 12.15 p.m., petitioner was riding the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JF-0240 carefully by observing traffic rules and regulations on the left side of the road.

When he was proceeding near Nymanahalli Village,
Nagamangala-Mysore road, Melkote Hobli, Pandavapura Taluk, Mandya District,
one Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-8154 came from Nagamangala side in a rash or negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.

Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained head injury right F-P Acute SDH, Type 2 open fracture left distal Tibia with medial malleolus fracture, fracture left distal fibula fracture and left clavicle mid 1/3rd.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Pandavapura, after first aid he was shifted to Apollo BGS Hospital, Mysore, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for one month.
X - rays
taken and C.T. scan was done.

The petitioner has undergone surgery like ORIF with plates and screws for clavicle left fracture on 29.10.2021, Surgery CRIF with IM Nail for fracture left tibia + square nail for lift fibula fracture + screws for left medial malleolus fracture and also right frontal/parietal burrhole and evacuation chronic done on 17.11.2021 and after conservative treatment he was discharged.
The petitioner was advised to take follow-up treatment, restricted fracture movements, not to involve in any straining activities and to take complete bed rest.

The petitioner has spend Rs.10,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
The doctors have advised him to undergo one more surgery for which he needs huge amount.

Further, the injuries sustained by the petitioner are not united, he is getting unbearable pain often,
he cannot walk, stand, lift weight and he is undergone deep mental shock.
The petitioner getting giddiness and he cannot concentrate on his work.
The injuries caused are permanent in nature.
The petitioner was aged 46 years at the time of accident and by doing agriculture work, he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month and contributed his entire income to the maintenance of family.
Due to injuries sustained by the petitioner, he has suffered financial hardship.

sentences.text: The accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-8154 by its driver and in this regard, Melkote police have registered the case against the driver of offending vehicle in Cr.No.144/2021 for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
The 1st respondent being the R.C. Owner and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of offending vehicle, hence both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, this petition.
3. After service of notice, 1st respondent being the R.C. Owner and 2nd respondent being the Insurer of offending vehicle appeared through their counsels and filed written statements.

4. The written statement averments of the 1st respondent are as hereunder:
The 1st respondent has denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Further denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner due to accident, rash and negligent driving of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW- 8154 by its driver.
Further denied the treatment taken by the petitioner and amount spent towards treatment.
Inter- alia the 1st respondent has contended that, insurance policy with respect to offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04- MW-8154 was valid as on the date of accident.
On the date of accident he was driving the said vehicle by holding valid D.L. and the said vehicle is having valid F.C.
Hence, the 2nd respondent is liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

5. The written statement averments of the 2nd respondent are as hereunder:
The 2nd respondent has denied the issuance of insurance policy with respect to vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-8154.
Further denied the involvement of offending vehicle in the alleged accident.
Inter-alia it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties viz., insurer/insured of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JF-0240.
The insured has violated the mandatory provisions under Sec.134(c) of M.V.Act by not submitting the vehicle documents.
The accident was occurred due to rash or negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JF-0240 by the petitioner.
The petitioner was not wearing helmet with ISI mark and he was not holding valid D.L., hence he himself contributed negligence for causing injuries.

The offending vehicle is not having valid and effective fitness certificate and permit, the driver of said vehicle was not holding valid D.L., as on the date of accident, hence, the insured has violated the terms and conditions of the policy by handed over his vehicle to the said person.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

10. According to the petitioner, he has sustained injuries in the road accident.
According to the 2 nd respondent-Insurance company, the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-8154 was not involved in the accident and no valid F.C. and permit to the said vehicle as on the date of accident.
According to the respondents the accident was occurred due to rash or negligent riding of the motor cycle by the petitioner and he was not wearing helmet with ISI Mark.
However, the respondents have not adduced evidence in this regard.
11. To prove the alleged negligence on the part of petitioner, the Insurance Company has cross-examined the petitioner/P.W.1 in detail.

At the cost of repetition, to substantiate its contention, Insurance company has not placed positive evidence.

12. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that when the petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 02-JF-0240, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW- 8154 came in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.
The evidence placed on record is clearly reveals that driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MW-8154 has caused the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.2:- This issue is with respect to age and income of the petitioner.
Age:- According to the petitioner, he was aged 46 years as on the date of accident.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.7 viz., the notarized copy of his Aadhaar Card.
On perusal of this document it appears to this Tribunal that, the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 01.01.1973.
The accident was occurred on 28.10.2021.
Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 48 years.
Accordingly, the age of the petitioner is considered as 48 years.
16. Income:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he was an agriculturist and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Per-contra, the 1 st and 2nd respondents have denied the income of petitioner.
To substantiate the income of petitioner, he has not placed any documentary evidence.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
"
In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".

17. In the absence of authentic document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the petitioner is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 28.10.2021.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2021 is Rs.15,000/- per month.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered in the Partly Affirmative.

19. ISSUE No.3:-

20. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-
(Income X year X Multiplier X Disability)

In the instant case, the petitioner has averred that, he has sustained grievous injuries like head injury F-P acute SDH and type-2 open fracture left distal tibia with medial malleolus fracture with fracture left distal fibula fracture and left clavicle mid 1/3rd.
He has produced wound certificate and discharge summary, which are marked as Ex.P.5 and Ex.P.8.

On perusal of these documents, it reveal that, the petitioner has sustained head injury right F-P acute SDH, type-2 open fracture left distal tibia with medial malleolus fracture with fracture left distal fibula, fracture left clavicle mid 1/3 rd.

It is relevant to mention that, respondent No.2 has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1.
21.

He has deposed that, on examination he found that, the petitioner walks with pain and limping using an elbow crutch, wasting of left thigh and calf diffuse swelling on left ankle is seen, surgical scars are seen over left knee leg and left clavicle and secondary scars are seen over right ankle.
X- ray shows united fracture of left clavicle with implants in situ, united fractures of distal tibia and fibula with implants in situ and united fracture of medial malleolus with implants in situ.

24. On perusal of the discharge summary of petitioner and evidence of medical witness coupled with wound certificate clearly reveals that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury and suffered physical disability.
However, considering the avocation of petitioner, the physical disability assessed by the P.W.3 is on higher side.
Hence, this Tribunal is considered the physical disability of the injured as 17% to the whole body.
25. As discussed supra, age of the injured is considered as 48 years and his income is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Annual income comes to Rs.1,80,000/-(15,000 x 12).
Hence, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of injured as per Sarala Verma case is 13.
If we multiplied yearly income with proper multiplier (1,80,000X 13), then it comes to Rs.23,40,000/-.
Already this Tribunal has considered the disability of petitioner as 19% to the whole body.
The same amount of Rs.3,97,800/- is awarded to the Injured/Petitioner under the head of loss of Future Income due to disabiltiy.

28. Pain and suffering:-

According to the petitioner, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Government Hospital, Pandavapura, after first aid he was shifted to Apollo BGS Hospital, Mysore,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for one month.

Already this Tribunal has observed that,
the petitioner has taken certain treatment.
In order to substantiate his contention, he has produced Ex.P.8, 9, 10 and Ex.P.27, the four Discharge summaries.

On perusal of these discharge summaries,
it reveals that, the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 28.10.2021 to 03.11.2021 for the first time for 8 days as per Ex.P.8.
As per Ex.P.9 from 16.11.2021 to 19.11.2021 for the second time for 4 days.
As per Ex.P.10 one day i.e., on 08.02.2022 for third time.
As per Ex.P.27, from 28.09.2023 to 30.09.2023 for the forth time for 3 days.
In total he has taken treatment as an inpatient for 16 days.
As per wound certificate coupled with discharge summaries, the petitioner has sustained injuries.
Further as per the evidence of doctor, it appears to this tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained physical disability.
There is no serious dispute with regard to inpatient for 16 days on four occasions.
As such, the petitioner suffered a lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal grants compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

29. Loss of income during the laidup period:-
The petitioner has produced discharge summary and same has been marked as Ex.P.8, 9, 10 and 27.

On perusal of these documents, it appear to this Tribunal that,
the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for 16 days.
However, the petitioner has not produced documents to show that, how many days he has taken bed rest.
Naturally it shows that, he might have taken atleast three months rest because of the injuries.
He has averred that, he was an agriculturist and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
But he has not produced documents to substantiate the same.
Hence, this Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Hence, three months is to be considered as loss of income during laidup period.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.45,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.

sentences.text: Food, Nourishment, conveyance and Atttendant charges:-

In so for as food, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatinet for about 16 days i.e., from 28.10.2021 to 03.11.2021, from 16.11.2021 to 19.11.2021 on 08.02.2022 and from 28.09.2023 to 30.09.2023.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents in this regard.

The petitioner has produced the bills at Sl.No.61 to 73 issued by S.N.G.
Tours and Travel pertaining to travelling charges and bills at Sl.No.3,4,12 and 15 pertaining to ambulance charges, which are covered in Ex.P.12.
The petitioner has not examined the person issued the said bills i.e., Sl.No.61 to 73.

Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of Food, Nourishment, conveyance and Atttendant charges.

31. Loss of future amenities and happiness:- The petitioner was aged about 48 years at the time of accident. The disability are physical deformity with which the petitionr has to live the rest of his life.
Therefore, he might have suffered pain, discomforts in life and loss of amenities.
By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disabiltiy, Rs.30,000/- is awarded under this head.
32. Future medical expenses:- P.W.1 has stated that, the doctors have advised him to undergo one more surgery, for which he needs huge amount.
On 20.01.2023, in his examination-in-chief, P.W.3 the medical witness has stated that, the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants, which will cost Rs.50,000/-.
On peursal of Ex.P.27, it reveals that, P.W.1 was admitted to Venus Multispeciality Hospital as an inpatient from 28.09.2023 to 30.09.2023 for the removal of implants of left clavicle and left leg.
P.W.1 has already produced Ex.P.28, the medical bills related to removal of implants.
On perusal of Ex.P.27, it can be inferred that, implant has been removed.
